incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC #1859004321 — Smart routing fallback loop detected — high error rate from eu-west-1 -> paging on-call

SRE-ONCALL: got the page, seeing ~1200 5xxs in last 3m from eu-west-1. Errors look like mismatch when runtime tries to fallback to quantized variant.

ALICE-ML: confirming, logs show model selection returned gptx-4-8q (8-bit quant) but the route metadata for the customer requires tool_calling and >32k context. 8q variant was registered with context_limit=8k and tools.enabled=false.

BOB-RUNTIME: that would cause tokenization/kvcache truncation mismatch and the exec layer to throw OOM-ish errors then 502. stack trace snippet: ```RuntimeError: KVCache length mismatch: expected 32768 got 8192```

CARLA-ROUTING: routing policies were updated in last rollout — we pushed a change that allows cheaper quant variants as fallback for cost-tiered routes. looks like the compatibility matrix had a missing entry for tool_calling support and context length.

DAVE-NIGHT-ONCALL: @sre-oncall I'm on this. Immediate mitigation?

SRE-ONCALL: First mitigation I'd prefer: disable smart-routing fallback to quant variants for eu-west-1 until we have a guard. Running command to flip policy: ```/infra toggle smart-routing eu-west-1 fallback_quant false```

DEPLOY-BOT: deploy triggered by @sre-oncall: /infra toggle smart-routing eu-west-1 fallback_quant false — started — 2 workers to roll — ETA 30s

NORA-CS: customer impact — we have two paying customers in eu-west-1 serving live chat with degraded responses; reported latency spikes and some hallucinated structured outputs. They've been notified via support channel and we gave temporary guidance to throttle.

EMILY-DEVEX: note for playbook — we should include tool_calling and context_limit in the compatibility matrix check before any routing decision. Right now the check only considers model_arch and max_seq.

ALICE-ML: quick reproduction: local route selection script picks variant list [gptx-4-fp16, gptx-4-8q]. The fallback logic currently only checks `is_variant_servable` which returns true for 8q because GPU is available. Should instead call `is_compatible(request,variant)` that validates `tools.enabled` and `context_limit >= request.context_len`.

BOB-RUNTIME: patch ready for runtime: ```diff
- if is_variant_servable(v): choose(v)
+ if is_variant_servable(v) and is_compatible(req,v): choose(v)
```

CARLA-ROUTING: after deploy-bot confirms toggle done — can we confirm error rate dropping?

DEPLOY-BOT: toggle completed — policy changed: fallback_quant=false for region eu-west-1 — rollout 100% in 22s

SRE-ONCALL: seeing error rate start to fall, 5xxs down to ~90/min. still some propagation left. :+1:

DAVE-NIGHT-ONCALL: I'll hold paging and start investigating why the compatibility matrix was incomplete. Handing lead to @alice-ml for model metadata changes.

ALICE-ML: looking into model registry — the 8q variant metadata file lacked `features: ["streaming","embeddings"]` and had `tools: false`. The 8q model was onboarded by infra earlier this month and missing the feature flags. Adding `tools:true` is not safe without retraining/validation. Will instead mark 8q as incompatible for tool_calling.

NORA-CS: do we have a list of customers affected and potential data exposure? They used function calls for payments processing. We need to confirm there were no partial calls.

BOB-RUNTIME: from logs, function-call events failed before execution, so no downstream calls were invoked. We have traces showing aborted tool_call attempts; good news: no external side-effects.

EMILY-DEVEX: temporary runbook update: add check at request admission time: if request.requires_tool_calling and variant.tools.enabled==false then do not select variant. Also add alert if fallback attempts > 3 in 60s.

CARLA-ROUTING: root cause: combinatorial gap between routing policy (cost-first fallback) and the compatibility matrix (which had sparse flags). Two fixes: 1) fast guard (policy disable) — done; 2) medium (runtime compatibility check) — ready to patch; 3) longer (update onboarding + validation and add matrix unit tests).

ALICE-ML: PR #4032 opened for registry validation to require `tools.enabled` and `context_limit` on all variants. Tests included. Tagging @bob-runtime for runtime change.

DEPLOY-BOT: PR #4032 build passed, negative tests added. Ready to merge after a short review.

SRE-ONCALL: can we schedule a quick canary for the runtime compatibility check? want to ensure no perf regression.

BOB-RUNTIME: yes — will roll to 2% of traffic in eu-west-1 then expand. Canary plan: ```
- 2% traffic, 10 minutes
- monitor 5xx, latency, mem
- rollback if 5xx>0.5% or mem increase >20%
```

DAVE-NIGHT-ONCALL: I'm going to keep an eye overnight, if things look stable I'll re-enable controlled fallbacks for non-tool routes only.

NORA-CS: notified affected customers with status updates. We'll offer account credits for the interval. CS will coordinate follow-up postmortem details.

EMILY-DEVEX: post-incident action items I'll own: update runbook, add unit tests to compatibility matrix, create an example snippet for onboarding docs showing `tools.enabled` flag.

ALICE-ML: follow-up: need to audit all quantized variants for context_limit < 32k and tools=false — will produce a list by EOD.

CARLA-ROUTING: long-term: change routing policy language to `fallback_criteria: [cost,latency]` and require `compatibility=TRUE` as mandatory.

SRE-ONCALL: current status — incident mitigated, error rate declining, no external side-effects detected. Will keep thread open for postmortem notes. Marking P0 -> P1 for follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident status updated to "mitigated" — on-call acknowledged — incident channel will remain until postmortem.

DAVE-NIGHT-ONCALL: handing off to morning oncall @alice-ml for follow-up and postmortem write-up. I'll add timeline notes to the ticket.

ALICE-ML: acknowledged, will draft a short blameless postmortem and link model registry diff + routing policy diffs.

NORA-CS: will send affected customers the summary and next steps timeline.

END OF THREAD: logs, traces, and PR links to be attached to the incident ticket.
